data.name: CredentialAttributesExplain
data.value: These hold credential material and are never managed by JIM. Passwords are synchronized through JIM's dedicated password channel, which writes to the Connected System without ever reading the value back into the Metaverse.

data.name: ActionRequiredText
data.value: Some attributes that were removed are still referenced by Synchronization Rules. Please update your Synchronization Rules to remove references to these attributes.

data.name: DataTypeLockedPlural
data.value: The data type and plurality of this Connected System attribute cannot be changed as it is being referenced by either a Synchronization Rule, or has values already populated.

data.name: DataTypeLocked
data.value: The data type of this Connected System attribute cannot be changed as it is being referenced by either a Synchronization Rule, or has values already populated.

data.name: ChooseObjectTypesHelp
data.value: Each type you select gets its own tab above, where you choose the attributes to import or export. To maximize system performance, select only the types you actually need.

data.name: AttributeSelectionHelp
data.value: Select which attributes you would like JIM to import, or export for this object type. To maximize system performance, only select those you actually need.

data.name: CredentialAttributeTooltip
data.value: This attribute holds credential material and cannot be managed by JIM. Passwords are synchronized through JIM's dedicated password channel, which writes to the Connected System without ever reading the value back into the Metaverse; they never flow through an Attribute Flow.

data.name: SkippedCredentialAttributes
data.value: Skipped {0}: credential attributes cannot be managed by JIM. Passwords are synchronized through JIM's dedicated password channel, not through Attribute Flow.

data.name: RefreshCancelled
data.value: Hierarchy refresh canceled. Nothing was changed.

data.name: PreviewReclassifiedBody
data.value: Applying this refresh can change {0}. By default, each object that would change Object Type is refused at the next import and reported as an {1} error; JIM keeps it exactly as it is, so nothing is deprovisioned. If the change is intended, run a Full Import Run Profile with {2} enabled to carry it out. Canceling keeps the current classification.

data.name: PreviewSyncRuleWord
data.value: Synchronization Rule

data.name: PreviewActionRequiredText
data.value: Some attributes that are no longer reported are still referenced by Synchronization Rules. Please update your Synchronization Rules to remove references to these attributes.

data.name: PreviewObsoletedBody
data.value: Obsoleted objects flow through the standard deprovisioning pipeline on the next synchronization run: disconnection, attribute recall, grace periods and Metaverse Deletion Rules all apply as configured.

data.name: PreviewCancelBody
data.value: Canceling does not preserve the status quo. The next Full Import will find no objects of a removed Object Type and obsolete them regardless, and the source now sends redefined attributes in their new form, so mappings validated against the old definition may misbehave. You can re-run the refresh at any time to decide.

data.name: DataFlowIntro
data.value: Every attribute data flow configured across all Connected Systems, in both directions. Use it to answer "where does this attribute's value come from, and what writes it out?" without opening each Synchronization Rule.

data.name: MultipleContributorsTooltip
data.value: Show only Inbound flows whose Metaverse Attribute is fed by more than one Synchronization Rule. This is a normal arrangement; it is simply where the priority order decides which value wins.

data.name: SearchScopeText
data.value: Search matches Synchronization Rules, Connected Systems, object types, attribute names on either side, and expression text. The attribute filters cannot match a flow whose relevant side is an expression, because an expression's attribute references live in its text; search finds those.

data.name: PriorityColumnTooltip
data.value: Where an Inbound flow sits in the order of everything contributing to the same Metaverse Attribute, 1 being highest. It only decides anything where more than one Synchronization Rule contributes, which is what the emphasized rows are.

data.name: DisabledRuleTooltip
data.value: This Synchronization Rule is disabled, so this flow is configured but moves no data.
